chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Ya'qub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Abu Kahmas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the first two rak'ahs, when I sit in them for the Tashahhud, and I say: 'Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings,' as a dismissal (ansirafan). He said: 'No, but when you say: 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah,' that is the dismissal.'

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأُولَيَيْنِ: The first two rak'ahs of the prayer
key_terms.لِلتَّشَهُّدِ: For the Tashahhud (sitting and reciting testimonies)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct phrase for ritual dismissal (ansiraf) during the Tashahhud in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the greeting of the Prophet and the ritual conclusion (ansiraf) of the prayer, establishing that the phrase 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah' serves as the valid dismissal. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential preference for this specific formula over the later popularized 'Attahiyat' text in the first sitting, emphasizing the communal aspect of the greeting to all righteous servants of Allah.
